title: Copilot Notebooks: JPG and PNG files as knowledge sources
summary: The briefing passes: the rollout facts, licensing statements, Cloud Policy path and preview Graph automation are supported. One descriptive statement overstates what the sources establish about who can see generated outputs; remove the claim that the user's sharing alone decides their audience.

claims.quote: IT administrators can control creation and use of Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks through Cloud Policy settings.

claims.claim: The setting is reached in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center through Customization > Policy Management > policy configuration > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks.

Select Customization from the left pane.
Select Policy Management.
Create a new policy configuration or edit an existing one.
From the Choose the scope dropdown list ...
In Configure Settings ... Create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks

claims.claim: TCM remediation and applyOnce are preview capabilities in Microsoft Graph beta.
claims.quote: Tenant Configuration Management (TCM) drift remediation and applyOnce monitors change workload configuration on behalf of the signed-in administrator. These capabilities are available in preview through Microsoft Graph beta.

claims.claim: The request's mode property must be applyOnce to apply the baseline once.
claims.quote:
The monitor mode. The possible values are: monitorOnly, applyOnce, unknownFutureValue. Optional; defaults to monitorOnly.
An active applyOnce monitor runs in the background on behalf of the signed-in administrator and then becomes inactive.

claims.claim: TCM supports this Copilot setting only in tenant-level policies.
claims.quote: The 20 Copilot resources are Office Cloud Policy Service (OCPS) settings. TCM supports these settings only in tenant-level policies in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.

claims.claim: A group-level configuration of the target setting causes TCM operations including applyOnce to fail for that resource.
claims.quote: Before using TCM, ensure that the target setting isn't configured in any group-level policy in that admin center. If it is, monitoring, snapshots, remediation, and applyOnce fail for that resource.

claims.claim: The calling application needs delegated ConfigurationMonitoring.ReadWrite.All for applyOnce.
claims.quote: Creating an applyOnce monitor supports delegated permissions only. In addition to the calling app's delegated ConfigurationMonitoring.ReadWrite.All permission, the TCM service principal needs delegated permissions for the target workloads

claims.claim: The TCM service principal needs delegated CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite.
claims.quote: For remediation and applyOnce, grant it the CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite delegated permission.

claims.claim: The signed-in administrator needs the AI Administrator role for this resource's applyOnce operation.
claims.quote: For remediation and applyOnce, AI Administrator is the least-privileged Microsoft Entra role for the signed-in user. This role requirement applies to the user, not to the TCM service principal.
